name: VoiceStudio
tagline: A free voice studio on your own computer: clone a voice, dub a video, or dictate in 646 languages - nothing uploaded.
sentence: Record a short sample of any voice, and VoiceStudio clones it on your machine so you can make it say new things, dub a video into another language, or turn text into a spoken audiobook - all without an internet connection.
replaces: ElevenLabs ($5-99/month subscription for cloud voice cloning and text-to-speech)

visual.alt: VoiceStudio's voice cloning screen: a sidebar with Clone, Design, Saved, Gallery, Stories, Dubbing, Transcribe, Projects, Tools and Integrations, and a main panel showing 'VoiceStudio Demo Voice' with a script input area reading 'Every voice has a story. Bring yours to life with VoiceStudio' and a pink 'Synthesize audio' button.
visual.caption: VoiceStudio's voice cloning view, from its own README: type text, pick a cloned voice, click Synthesize.

board.say: You want to clone a voice or make a voiceover, but cloud services charge a monthly fee and upload your recordings to someone else's servers.
board.eg: ElevenLabs, the best-known voice cloning service, starts at $5/month and processes everything on their cloud servers.

board.say: You open the VoiceStudio app on your computer and pick what you want to do: clone, design, dub, transcribe or dictate.
board.eg: Double-click the app icon, or type `voicestudio` in a terminal. The interface opens in a window.

board.say: A voice recording to clone, a video to dub, or text to speak aloud.
board.eg: A 30-second recording of your voice, plus the text you want it to say in any of 646 supported languages.

board.say: It runs AI voice models entirely on your computer to clone, generate or transcribe speech.
steps: For cloning: it analyzes your voice sample and builds a voice profile that captures how you sound
For text-to-speech: it reads your text and generates audio in the cloned voice, adjusting speed, pitch and emotion
For dubbing: it transcribes a video's audio, translates it, and re-speaks it in the new language using the original speaker's cloned voice
board.eg: The README's demo: record a sample, type a sentence, click 'Synthesize audio,' and hear it spoken back in your cloned voice.

board.say: Audio files, dubbed videos, or live dictation - all made locally, no data leaving your machine.

outputs.what: A cloned voice that speaks your text
outputs.eg: An audio file of your voice saying something you never recorded, in any of 646 languages
Your English video re-spoken in Spanish, with the original speaker's voice preserved
Spoken audio turned into a written transcript you can search and edit

before: Voice cloning means a cloud subscription, uploading sensitive recordings to a company's server, and usage limits tied to your plan.
Dubbing a video into another language means hiring a voice actor or using a service that charges per minute of audio.
after: Clone any voice on your own computer - free, unlimited, no recordings leave your machine.
Dub a video into another language in minutes, keeping the original speaker's voice, without paying per minute or per word.
uses_note: VoiceStudio is about 6 months old with 51K+ stars and active development (2,496 pull requests). Named public uses are hard to find - most users share results (audio clips) rather than crediting the tool.

pulse.history_note: Created Apr 9. The 30-day gain of +38K is from findarepo's measured data.

steps: [Download VoiceStudio](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) from GitHub Releases - pick the installer for your system (Mac, Windows or Linux).
Inside the app, select Voice > Clone. Record a 30-second sample of your voice (or anyone's), then type a sentence you want it to say.
Click 'Synthesize audio' and listen to the result. Then try the Dubbing tab with a short video clip.

If that scan passes: download the app, clone a voice from a sample, synthesize a sentence, and report how it sounds. Try one more feature (dubbing or transcription). 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: No data found for the exact install size. Voice models typically run 1-5 GB each; the app downloads models on first use.
footprint.memory: No data found for a specific number. Voice AI models generally need 4-8 GB of RAM. A graphics card speeds things up but isn't strictly required.
footprint.runs_on: Mac, Windows, Linux. Desktop app (Electron-based). The README mentions Twilio, Plivo and n8n integrations for phone and automation workflows.

best_for: You want to clone a voice or make voiceovers without paying a subscription or uploading recordings to the cloud
You need to dub videos into other languages and want to keep the original speaker's voice
skip_if: You need the absolute best voice quality for a commercial product - ElevenLabs' cloud models are still ahead for production-grade output
You don't have a reasonably modern computer - running voice AI locally needs decent hardware

alternatives.name: ElevenLabs
alternatives.line: The cloud voice-cloning leader, $5-99/month. Higher quality and easier to start, but your recordings are processed on their servers.

alternatives.name: Coqui TTS
alternatives.line: An older open-source text-to-speech project. VoiceStudio bundles more features (dubbing, transcription, a desktop app) in one package.

watch: **Quality may not match ElevenLabs.** Local voice models are improving fast, but cloud services with larger models and more training data still produce more natural-sounding output.
**Model downloads on first use.** The app downloads AI models when you first use each feature, which can take a while on a slow connection.
**Voice cloning raises ethical questions.** Cloning someone's voice without their permission is easy with this tool. The tool doesn't enforce any consent checks.
**One main developer.** Active development (2,496 PRs) but sustained by a single maintainer.
